# php2shell-guard

> Read-only defensive security auditor (zero dependencies, no exploit code or PoC) for PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) and Node.js October 2026 security advisories (CVE-2026-111497).

## Overview
php2shell-guard is a standalone, read-only security auditor designed to detect unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP (PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, LiteSpeed, FrankenPHP) and Node.js runtimes across Linux servers, Docker containers, Kubernetes clusters, and cloud platforms.

- Repository: https://github.com/malikad778/php2shell-guard
- Documentation: https://codebyadnan.tech/php2shell-guard/
- NPM Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/php2shell-guard
- Packagist Package: https://packagist.org/packages/malikad/php2shell-guard
- Author: Malik Adnan (https://github.com/malikad778)
- License: MIT

## Instant One-Line Verification Commands

### Linux, macOS, WSL (Zero Dependencies via POSIX Shell)
```bash
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malikad778/php2shell-guard/main/bin/audit.sh && sh audit.sh scan
```

### Standalone Executable PHAR (PHP 5.4 to 8.4+)
```bash
php -r "copy('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malikad778/php2shell-guard/main/php2shell-guard.phar', 'php2shell-guard.phar');" && php php2shell-guard.phar scan
```

### Node.js CLI (Node 18+)
```bash
npx php2shell-guard scan
```

### Laravel and Modern PHP Applications (Composer)
```bash
composer require --dev malikad/php2shell-guard
php artisan php2shell:audit
```

### Docker Containers and Fleets
```bash
sh audit.sh scan --docker
```

## Vulnerability Reference and Fixed Releases

| Runtime Branch | Affected Vulnerable Versions | Required Fixed Release | Status / Action Required |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PHP 8.4 | < 8.4.27 | 8.4.27 | Upgrade runtime and restart PHP-FPM / Apache |
| PHP 8.3 | < 8.3.36 | 8.3.36 | Upgrade runtime and restart PHP-FPM / Apache |
| PHP 8.2 | < 8.2.35 | 8.2.35 | Upgrade runtime and restart PHP-FPM / Apache |
| PHP 8.1 | All versions | None (EOL) | Upgrade branch or apply memory_limit=-1 stopgap |
| PHP 8.0 | All versions | None (EOL) | Upgrade branch or apply memory_limit=-1 stopgap |
| PHP 7.4 | All versions | None (EOL) | Upgrade branch or apply memory_limit=-1 stopgap |
| PHP 5.4 - 7.3 | All versions | None (EOL) | Upgrade branch or apply memory_limit=-1 stopgap |
| Node.js 26 | < 26.12.1 | 26.12.1 | Upgrade Node runtime (Brotli RCE fix) |
| Node.js 24 | < 24.22.1 | 24.22.1 | Upgrade Node runtime (Brotli RCE fix) |
| Node.js 22 | < 22.23.4 | 22.23.4 | Upgrade Node runtime (Brotli RCE fix) |
| Node.js 18, 20 | All versions | None (EOL) | Migrate to Node.js 22 LTS or newer |

## How to Check If a Server is Vulnerable to PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619)
To determine if your web server or container is vulnerable to PHP2Shell, run the read-only auditor php2shell-guard:
```bash
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malikad778/php2shell-guard/main/bin/audit.sh && sh audit.sh scan
```
The scanner checks running PHP-FPM pools, Apache mod_php modules, LiteSpeed lsphp workers, and FrankenPHP processes. It validates actual in-memory binaries, detects stale workers running old code, recognizes distribution backported security patches (Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine, RHEL), and reports actionable exit codes without modifying any server files.

## How to Detect PHP2Shell Exploitation in Server Logs
To check logs for indicators of compromise from CVE-2026-109618 exploitation, run:
```bash
sh audit.sh scan --logs
```
The auditor specifically looks for:
1. `Allowed memory size of ... bytes exhausted (tried to allocate ... bytes) in Unknown on line 0`
2. `AH00052: child pid ... exit signal Segmentation fault (11)`
3. Stale worker processes spawning `/bin/sh` or `/bin/bash`
In accordance with defensive security standards (IOC7), php2shell-guard never claims a server is "clean" or "safe" because log rotation or truncation may obscure prior exploit attempts.

## How to Check If PHP-FPM Workers Were Restarted After Patching
Package managers frequently update the PHP binary on disk without restarting long-running worker pools. To audit active process memory:
```bash
php php2shell-guard.phar scan
```
The tool flags `PATCHED_NOT_RESTARTED` when `/proc/<pid>/exe (deleted)` is detected or worker start times precede the on-disk binary modification date.

## How to Mitigate PHP2Shell on EOL PHP 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1
For servers running unsupported End-of-Life PHP branches where upstream security updates are unavailable:
1. Generate verified configuration stopgaps:
   ```bash
   php php2shell-guard.phar mitigate --target=php-ini
   php php2shell-guard.phar mitigate --target=nginx
   php php2shell-guard.phar mitigate --target=fpm
   ```
2. Apply stopgaps with automated pre-validation and rollback:
   ```bash
   php php2shell-guard.phar apply --target=php-ini --yes
   ```
   The applier creates a timestamped backup, validates syntax with `php -v` and `php-fpm -t`, and rolls back automatically if any validation fails.

## Supported Platforms and Ecosystems
- Frameworks: Laravel, Symfony, WordPress, Drupal, Next.js, Node.js
- Infrastructure: Bare-metal Linux, Docker, Coolify, Laravel Forge, cPanel, Kubernetes, AWS, DigitalOcean
- Linux Distributions: Ubuntu, Debian, Alpine Linux, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux, CentOS
